meta.description: Invariant descriptors are provably blind: homometric (Z-related) neighbour sets share every two- and three-body quantity and the whole power spectrum, but differ at l=2 equivariantly.

checks.name: both configs have every neighbour at r = 1
sorted centre-neighbour distance multisets are bitwise identical
24-channel Gaussian two-body descriptor is bitwise identical
Stillinger-Weber three-body energy differs by > 10x
l=1 power separates them (0 for the triangle by symmetry)
A and B are both all-interval tetrachords <1,1,1,1,1,1>
all centre-neighbour distances equal 1 in both
sorted neighbour-neighbour distance multisets agree (homometry)
sorted bond-angle-cosine multisets agree (so every 3-body term is blind)
A and B are NOT in the same dihedral orbit of Z_12 (exact, 24 symmetries)
brute-force min RMSD over 24 perms x 3601 angles x reflection is >> 0
the fine scan reproduces the exact 2-D closed form
full O(3) Kabsch over perms finds nothing better (no out-of-plane escape)
min RMSD equals the closed form (sqrt(3)-1)/2
feature map is equivariant: f_l(R X) = D^l(R) f_l(X), l = 0..6
l = 0 features are identical
l = 1 is the lowest degree whose lab-frame features differ
invariant power spectrum p_l is BLIND at every l = 0..6
addition theorem p_l = (2l+1)/4pi sum_jk P_l(cos theta_jk) holds
l <= 1 does NOT separate: an explicit rotation aligns f_1 exactly
that same R* leaves l = 2 badly mismatched
l <= 2 DOES separate: certified lower bound on min_R mismatch is > 0
SO(3) search agrees with the certificate and finds no near-alignment
CG bispectrum separates A and B where the power spectrum cannot
parity-odd bispectrum entries vanish for both (planar = achiral)
